claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-3:DonHang.Domain/NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents.cs: 15 OrderPlaced -> "order.placed", 17 "order.cancelled", 19 "order.shipped", 21/23/25 refund events; 34 `outbox.Add(routingKey, new OrderMessage(order.Id, customer.Email, customer.FullName, domainEvent.OccurredAt))`. OrderMessage.cs: `record OrderMessage(int OrderId, string CustomerEmail, string CustomerName, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt)`. No RabbitMQ or SaveChanges in the handler.

Carried from round 1 (section unchanged): OrderService.cs 49 `await events.DispatchAsync(order);` 50 `await repository.SaveChangesAsync();`, same pair in every use case; EfOrderRepository.SaveChangesAsync is one `db.SaveChangesAsync()`.

git show stage-3:DonHang.Infrastructure/EfOutbox.cs matches the block; 12 ctor takes DonHangDbContext, 16 `db.OutboxMessages.Add`, 18 RoutingKey, 19 `JsonSerializer.Serialize(message, message.GetType(), JsonSerializerOptions.Web)`; no SaveChanges call. Docs, web defaults: "PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase"; "In .NET 9 and later versions, you can use the JsonSerializerOptions.Web singleton".

"By default, if the database provider supports transactions, all changes in a single call to `SaveChanges` are applied in a transaction. If any of the changes fail, then the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied to the database."

Carried from round 1: OutboxMessage.cs:11 `public Guid Id { get; init; } = Guid.NewGuid();` 22 `public DateTimeOffset? PublishedAt { get; set; }`; DonHangDbContext.cs:125 `ToTable("outbox_messages")`, 126-131 id, routing_key, body jsonb, created_at, published_at, trace_parent. Lesson now says only 'maps these to columns of outbox_messages'.

Carried from round 1: docker-compose.yml:158 api `Database=donhang`; :316 notifications `Database=donhang_notifications`; DonHangDbContext.cs:99-101 Payments/Notifications rows live "in their own databases"; RabbitMqTopology.cs:12 `Queue = "notifications.order-events"`.

NotifyCustomerOnOrderEvents.cs @ stage-3 line 33 `?? throw new InvalidOperationException(...)` (prose line number matches); DispatchAsync awaits handlers without catch; OrderService.cs:49-50 dispatch precedes SaveChangesAsync, so the save is skipped.

Claim, lesson section 6 and quiz q2 now carry the condition ('with no transaction opened around them as in Đơn Hàng'). Docs: one SaveChanges call is one transaction by default; "You can use the `DbContext.Database` API to begin, commit, and rollback transactions" to span several. Đơn Hàng opens none.

EfOutbox.Add only adds to the context; IOutbox.cs @ stage-3 :6-7 "the caller's SaveChangesAsync saves it with the order, and OutboxRelay publishes it afterwards. Nothing is sent here." OutboxRelay is a BackgroundService on a PeriodicTimer and alone sets PublishedAt (round 1 inspection).

Carried from round 1 (section unchanged): prereq backend.l2.database-job-queue quotes QueuedNotifier @ stage-2, `db.Notifications.Add` of a pending row in the order's DbContext; NotificationSender sends later.

Section 6 now says 'list RabbitMQ's queues'. RabbitMQ management docs: the UI can "Declare, list and delete exchanges, queues, bindings...". RabbitMqTopology.cs:12 `Queue = "notifications.order-events"`; no outbox queue is declared; outbox_messages is a PostgreSQL table (claim 5).

Ran `git -C examples/don-hang grep -n SaveChangesAsync stage-3 -- <3 files>` -> exactly two lines: `stage-3:DonHang.Domain/IOutbox.cs:6:// DonHang.Infrastructure); the caller's SaveChangesAsync saves it with the` and `stage-3:DonHang.Infrastructure/EfOutbox.cs:9:// as the order, and saves nothing: OrderService's SaveChangesAsync writes the`. Both comments.

Rationale supported by code: OutboxRelay re-reads rows with `published_at IS NULL` each tick and catches failures to retry (OutboxRelay.cs:21-30); partial index `HasFilter("published_at IS NULL")` (DonHangDbContext.cs:132).

git show stage-3 ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs: 17 `services.AddDbContext<DonHangDbContext>(...)`, 18 `AddScoped<IOrderRepository, EfOrderRepository>()`, 24 `AddScoped<IOutbox, EfOutbox>()`. EF docs: "The `AddDbContext` extension method registers `DbContext` types with a scoped lifetime by default."

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed sentence). 'as in Đơn Hàng' sits right after 'with no transaction opened around them', so on first read I took it to mean Đơn Hàng does open one. I also did not know a transaction can be opened around two saves; the lesson only shows one SaveChangesAsync as one transaction. I re-read it twice, but the point (two saves, two transactions) still came through.
issues.quote: Actually two calls, with no transaction opened around them as in Đơn Hàng, are two transactions,
issues.fix: Reorder: 'Actually, in Đơn Hàng, where nothing opens a transaction around them, two calls are two transactions, ...'. Apply the same order in quiz q2's explanation.
